title: Open a bean seed and find the baby plant
description: Inside a dry bean seed there is a tiny baby plant, all folded up and waiting. Soak a bean overnight, open it gently, and you can meet the plant before it even starts to grow.

body.heading: Soak and open
paragraphs: Put a big dried bean, like a kidney bean or butter bean, in water overnight. In the morning it will be fat and soft, and its skin will wrinkle like fingers after a long bath.
A grown-up helps you slip off the skin and gently open the bean into its two halves. Look inside: can you see a tiny pale sprout, curled up small? That is the baby plant.

body.heading: A packed lunch for a plant
paragraphs: The two big halves of the bean are the baby plant's packed lunch. When the seed starts to grow, the baby plant eats this food until its own leaves open and it can make food from sunlight.
You can draw the baby plant in a notebook, or take a photo with a grown-up's help. Then plant another soaked bean in a pot of soil and watch the real thing grow.

takeaway: A soaked bean opens into two halves — the baby plant's packed lunch — with a tiny folded sprout waiting inside.
ageGuidance: Ages 3-8: grown-up leads throughout; younger children watch and point while the grown-up opens the bean.
materials: Dried kidney beans or butter beans
A small pot and soil (optional, for planting afterwards)
supervision: A grown-up must soak, open and handle the beans; children help by looking, pointing and drawing.
safetyNotes: Raw dried kidney beans must never be eaten — they can make you very poorly. Beans in this activity are for looking and planting only.
Wash hands after handling soaked beans and soil.
Keep dried beans away from younger toddlers, who may put them in their mouths.
screenFreeExtension: Plant a soaked bean in soil by a sunny window and check it every morning for a week, drawing what changes.
